findings.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:46 uses `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` instead of `||`, making 'admin or owner' check effectively owner-only, so team admins get FORBIDDEN when adding guests to their team's bookings
addGuests.handler.ts:46 performs two sequential DB round-trips (isTeamAdmin then isTeamOwner) where one would suffice

MultiEmail.tsx imports from its own package @calcom/ui, creating a module cycle (index.tsx → MultiEmailLazy → MultiEmail → index.tsx) that degrades package usability outside the web app and negates the lazy-loading rationale by statically pulling the full barrel into its chunk

addGuests.handler.ts:81 duplicate-guest suppression is case-sensitive, so a guest already on the booking under different casing is inserted twice, causing duplicate emails and duplicate .ics attendee entries
addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check compares non-lowercased `guest` against lowercased blacklistedGuestEmails, allowing a blacklisted email to bypass the check via different casing
addGuests.handler.ts:170 catch block discards the error: console.log('Error sending AddGuestsEmails') never logs err, making SMTP/template failures invisible in production logs

Team permission check uses && instead of || in addGuests.handler.ts (~line 50), so isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner is always false (no member holds both roles), locking out team admins/owners and silently dropping admin-level guest management (P1, confidence 100)

Server schema ZAddGuestsInputSchema omits the uniqueness validation that the client dialog enforces, allowing duplicate emails in a single guests array to pass server validation and create duplicate attendee rows via createMany (P2, confidence 75)
No max-length bound on the guests array in the server schema, allowing unbounded guest counts and unbounded email fan-out (P2, confidence 75)
Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive: blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased but compared against raw guest strings, so 'User@Spam.com' bypasses a 'user@spam.com' blacklist entry (P2, confidence 75)

Attendee de-duplication check is case-sensitive: guest === attendee.email comparison allows 'Jane@X.com' to duplicate existing attendee 'jane@x.com', creating duplicate attendee rows and sending a second email (P2, confidence 75)

No booking.status check in the handler: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, generating ICS attachments with method REQUEST and status CONFIRMED that re-confirm dead events in attendees' calendars (P2, confidence 75)
No tests exist for the new mutation, dialogs, or email templates, leaving the new authorization boundary (permission matrix, blacklist filtering, de-duplication) unverified (P1, confidence 100)

hideCalendarNotes is missing from the constructed CalendarEvent evt, unlike the scheduled-booking flow, causing private descriptions to leak in guest-add ICS attachments for event types configured to hide calendar notes (ADVISORY, P2)

Handler ignores seat capacity and never creates bookingSeat records for seated event types, allowing guests to be added and emailed while overfilling the slot and desynchronizing seat counts (ADVISORY, P2)

Email send failure is swallowed with console.log and the mutation still returns success, so the organizer sees a success toast when no emails or ICS updates were sent, with no partial-success signal (ADVISORY, P3)

Calendar update runs with the calling user's credentials instead of the organizer's: when an attendee adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees executes with the attendee's calendar credentials against a calendar event they don't own, failing or being skipped while the DB write already committed (ADVISORY, P2)

Team-permission check uses && instead of ||: `isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId) && isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId)`; since a Membership has a single role, no user can be both ADMIN and OWNER, so team admins always get FORBIDDEN and the isTeamAdmin call is dead code (addGuests.handler.ts:42-44)

Handler grants mutation to any booking attendee and constructs EventManager with the caller's (ctx.user) credentials instead of the booking owner's, so an attendee can add guests and calendar updates run under the wrong account's credentials against the organizer's calendar reference (addGuests.handler.ts:46-51, 148-153)

Booking query filters only on id with no status check, and ICS status is hardcoded to CONFIRMED in both email classes, allowing guests to be added to cancelled/rejected bookings and sending ICS REQUESTs that resurrect cancelled events in calendars (addGuests.handler.ts:26-50, organizer-add-guests-email.ts:19-20, attendee-add-guests-email.ts:12-16)

Client and server schemas have drifted: the dialog's zod schema has a uniqueness .refine but ZAddGuestsInputSchema does not, and the handler only dedupes against existing attendees, never within the guests array, and compares case-sensitively while the blacklist lowercases; duplicate or case-variant emails insert duplicate Attendee rows causing duplicate ICS/email sends (addGuests.schema.ts:4-6, AddGuestsDialog.tsx:29-33, addGuests.handler.ts:59-66)

Blacklisted emails are silently filtered out while the handler still returns success and the dialog toasts guests_added, so the operator has no way to know some emails were dropped (addGuests.handler.ts:55-66)

For event types with seatsPerTimeSlot, createMany on attendees bypasses seat logic entirely, so seat caps are not enforced and recipients get AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the seat-booking email flow (addGuests.handler.ts:83-92)
The guests array is unbounded (z.array(z.string().email()) with no .max), allowing a single mutation to enqueue thousands of emails and createMany rows (addGuests.schema.ts:5)

Dialog initializes multiEmailValue to [""] and 'Add another' appends "", which fails z.string().email() validation, so one leftover empty row blocks submission of otherwise-valid input with a misleading uniqueness error (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:38-47, MultiEmail.tsx:78-92)
Email-send error handler swallows the error object entirely (`catch { console.log(...) }` with no error argument), making email-delivery outages undebuggable (addGuests.handler.ts:168-172)

addGuests.handler.ts:33-35 - Team-permission check ANDs isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, making the admin-or-owner gate unreachable for team ADMINs, causing them to receive FORBIDDEN when editing team bookings; should use || or a single role check

addGuests.handler.ts:60-84 - Guest dedupe compares raw input case-sensitively with no canonical form and no unique DB constraint on (bookingId, email), allowing format drift duplicates (e.g. Guest@X.com vs guest@x.com) that create duplicate attendee rows, ics REQUESTs, and emails
addGuests.handler.ts:60-84 - Check-then-insert dedupe has TOCTOU race: two concurrent addGuests calls can both observe the attendee absent and both insert duplicate attendee rows

addGuests.handler.ts:66-84 + addGuests.schema.ts:4 - Guests array has no .max() cap, allowing an unbounded guest list that materializes 10k+ attendee rows, emails, and calendar payload in a single user-triggered request

addGuests.handler.ts:16-24 - Booking fetch has no status guard and templates hardcode CONFIRMED/REQUEST, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, sending ics REQUEST emails that re-accept cancelled events on attendees' calendars

addGuests.handler.ts:150-155 - Calendar update uses the requesting user's credentials, so when an attendee (permitted via isAttendee branch) calls the mutation, updateCalendarAttendees runs with empty credentials and the organizer's calendar event attendee list never updates, diverging from the DB

AddGuestsDialog.tsx:15-18 - Dialog re-declares an inline zod schema instead of importing the shared ZAddGuestsInputSchema, and the copies already disagree on uniqueness semantics, risking client/server drift

addGuests.handler.ts:33-35 - Permission check performs two sequential DB round-trips (isTeamAdmin then isTeamOwner) hitting the same membership row; a single membership fetch resolving the role once would remove a query and prevent role-combination mistakes
Permission gate in addGuests.handler.ts allows any logged-in attendee of a booking to mutate it, not just the organizer or team admins, expanding the trust model without accepted intent (P1)

Calendar update in addGuests.handler.ts runs with the caller's credentials via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user), so when an attendee triggers the mutation, updateCalendarAttendees is invoked with the attendee's calendar credentials against the organizer's event, and the organizer's calendar never gets the new attendees (P1)

isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, requiring a user to be both admin and owner, effectively rejecting non-owner team admins while accepting any attendee; the permission hierarchy is inverted relative to the intended admin-or-owner pattern (P1)
Handler never checks booking.status, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings and receive hard-CONFIRMED REQUEST ics invites that re-confirm a cancelled meeting (P1)

Silent contract drift between client and server: server silently filters duplicate and blacklisted emails from guests and returns success, while the client enforces uniqueness and shows a success toast, so users are told guests were added when they were silently dropped (P2)

Email delivery failure in addGuests.handler.ts is swallowed with only a console.log after the DB write, so callers are told guests were added and the cache is invalidated even when guests receive no email or ics invite (P2)

AddGuestsDialog.tsx and addGuests.schema.ts maintain two independently hand-maintained Zod schemas for the same input that have already diverged (client has uniqueness refine, server doesn't), requiring future validation changes to be made twice (P3)

New guests are assigned timeZone and locale from the organizer rather than guest-derived values, so persisted attendee records carry misleading timezone data that future features trusting attendee.timeZone will inherit (P3)
Email blacklist normalization mismatch in addGuests.handler.ts: blacklist entries are lowercased but incoming guest email is compared un-normalized, allowing bypass via case variation
Authorization logic error in addGuests.handler.ts: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring callers to be both team admin AND team owner, blocking non-owner admins

Trust-the-client authz in addGuests.handler.ts: any attendee of any booking permanently retains add-guests rights with no booking.status check or cap, enabling emails with organizer identity and video-call URL to arbitrary addresses
Guests array is unbounded (z.array without max) and endpoint has no rate limit, creating an email-bombing vector against arbitrary third-party addresses
Server-side dedup of guests against existing attendees is case-sensitive and doesn't dedup within input, causing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate email sends
No booking.status check before mutating: guests can be added to cancelled or rejected bookings, sending REQUEST/CONFIRMED ics invites that silently resuscitate cancelled meetings

Client-side email validation schema in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is a duplicated copy of ZAddGuestsInputSchema, causing client/server drift risk and misleading BAD_REQUEST errors when they diverge; should import the shared schema instead

In AddGuestsDialog.tsx onError, the fallback `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` is dead code because the template string message is always non-empty, making the fallback toast unreachable; the condition should be restructured so the fallback is reachable

addGuests.handler.ts swallows all email send failures with a non-error console.log and still returns success, decoupling the success response from the email side effect; the catch should log the actual error and surface failure in the response

Dual-write gap: attendees are committed to the DB before the calendar update in addGuests.handler.ts:95-105, and a calendar failure leaves persisted state inconsistent with no rollback or compensation

Retry after a partial calendar failure is blocked: the dedupe filter (uniqueGuests) excludes emails already in booking.attendees, causing emails_must_be_unique_valid errors and wedging the feature for those guests (never added to calendar, never invited)
Email send failure is silently swallowed by catch with console.log, so guests can be persisted with no invite ever sent while the user is told 'Guests added'
Case-sensitive dedupe in addGuests.handler.ts:78-85 allows duplicate attendee rows for the same person; no unique constraint on (bookingId, email) in the base schema

Client-side Set check in AddGuestsDialog.tsx only dedupes within one dialog session, not against persisted attendees across sessions or case variants, so it doesn't mitigate the duplicate-attendee issue

Blacklisted/duplicate guests are silently dropped in addGuests.handler.ts:72-85 while the caller is told 'Guests added', a false organizer-facing success report (silent mismatch between reported and actual data)

New guests are written with name: "" and the organizer's timeZone/locale in addGuests.handler.ts:106-120, persisting incorrect data (wrong timezone) for the guest with no way to correct it, misclassifying the row from creation
addGuests.handler.ts:81-83 uses && instead of || for team admin/owner permission check, wrongly rejecting team admins who are not owners (and vice versa) with FORBIDDEN
addGuests.handler.ts:118-127 commits DB attendee write before calendar update with no rollback or error handling, leaving partial state on calendar failure
addGuests.handler.ts:88 dedup filter makes retries of failed calendar sync impossible — persisted guests are excluded so retry throws 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' BAD_REQUEST

addGuests.handler.ts:151-154 email failure silently swallowed with bare console.log (no error object, bookingId, or stack), user sees 'Guests added' success toast while no notifications or ICS updates were sent
AddGuestsDialog.tsx:41-44 error message template literal is always truthy, making the t('unable_to_add_guests') fallback dead code and showing 'undefined:' prefix toast on errors without data.code
addGuests.handler.ts:71-73 findFirstOrThrow on nullable booking.userId surfaces an unhandled Prisma P2025 500 error instead of the promised NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN/BAD_REQUEST TRPCError shapes
addGuests.handler.ts:158-163 EventManager built from acting user's credentials instead of the organizer's, so calendar update silently no-ops when a non-organizer adds guests while reporting success
addGuests.schema.ts:5 guests array has no .max() cap, allowing unbounded payload to amplify into N attendee rows, N emails, and per-attendee calendar writes
addGuests.handler.ts:86-94 dedup/blacklist email comparisons are case-sensitive while blacklist is lowercased, allowing duplicate attendees and blacklist bypass by changing case
Server schema does not enforce uniqueness within the guests input array, so direct API calls with duplicate strings insert duplicate rows via createMany
AddGuestsDialog.tsx:30-36 isInvalidEmail is never reset on success or dialog re-open, showing stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' warning over untouched input
organizer-add-guests-email.ts:30 replyTo header grows unboundedly with attendee count across repeated add-guests calls, eventually causing MTAs to reject or clip the message

goldens.comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.

The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.

The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.

uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which performs two awaited calls back-to-back (two DB round-trips if those helpers hit the DB). This is a real, diff-grounded performance/efficiency concern; it’s not a correctness defect by itself as stated in the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmail.tsx imports from its own package @calcom/ui, creating a module cycle (index.tsx → MultiEmailLazy → MultiEmail → index.tsx) that degrades package usability outside the web app and negates the lazy-loading rationale by statically pulling the full barrel into its chunk

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the component imports `Button, EmailField, Icon, Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui`, which is the same package barrel (`packages/ui/index.tsx`). The barrel now exports `MultiEmail` via `./form/MultiEmailLazy`, which dynamically imports `./form/MultiEmail`. This creates a circular dependency path shown in the diff: `index.tsx -> form/MultiEmailLazy.tsx -> form/MultiEmail.tsx -> @calcom/ui (index.tsx)`. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded architecture issue and can undermine the intended lazy-loading boundary by pulling the barrel into the MultiEmail chunk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:81 duplicate-guest suppression is case-sensitive, so a guest already on the booking under different casing is inserted twice, causing duplicate emails and duplicate .ics attendee entries

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the duplicate suppression compares emails with strict equality (`guest === attendee.email`) and blacklist check uses `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing case. Since the input `guests` are not lowercased, an existing attendee email with different casing (e.g., `Foo@Bar.com`) will not be detected and `createMany` will insert another attendee row, leading to duplicate attendee entries and downstream duplicate notifications/ICS attendee list.

This doesn’t break core booking/guest-add behavior, but it materially reduces diagnosability of SMTP/template failures introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema ZAddGuestsInputSchema omits the uniqueness validation that the client dialog enforces, allowing duplicate emails in a single guests array to pass server validation and create duplicate attendee rows via createMany (P2, confidence 75)
No max-length bound on the guests array in the server schema, allowing unbounded guest counts and unbounded email fan-out (P2, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: The new server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max(...)` (or similar) bound. The handler `addGuestsHandler` then uses this array to `createMany` attendees and to send emails in `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which iterates attendees and enqueues emails (`Promise.all(emailsToSend)`). This permits an unbounded guest count leading to potentially unbounded DB inserts and email fan-out/DoS risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist comparison is case-sensitive: blacklistedGuestEmails are lowercased but compared against raw guest strings, so 'User@Spam.com' bypasses a 'user@spam.com' blacklist entry (P2, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are normalized to lowercase (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the comparison uses the raw `guest` string: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `guest` is not lowercased/normalized, a mixed-case email like `User@Spam.com` would not match a blacklist entry `user@spam.com` and would bypass the blacklist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendee de-duplication check is case-sensitive: guest === attendee.email comparison allows 'Jane@X.com' to duplicate existing attendee 'jane@x.com', creating duplicate attendee rows and sending a second email (P2, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, de-duplication uses strict equality `guest === attendee.email` when filtering `uniqueGuests`, with no normalization (e.g., `.toLowerCase()`), so an existing attendee `jane@x.com` would not match an added guest `Jane@X.com`. This can lead to creating duplicate attendee rows via `createMany` and triggers email sending based on the unnormalized `newGuests` list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking.status check in the handler: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, generating ICS attachments with method REQUEST and status CONFIRMED that re-confirm dead events in attendees' calendars (P2, confidence 75)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` (new file `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`), the booking is loaded and updated without any guard on booking state (no `booking.status` / cancelled/rejected check) before (1) updating attendees in DB and (2) calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. The new email templates generate ICS with `method: "REQUEST"` and `status: "CONFIRMED"` (see `packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`), so invoking this mutation for a cancelled/rejected booking could send reconfirming calendar updates for an event that should be “dead”.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No tests exist for the new mutation, dialogs, or email templates, leaving the new authorization boundary (permission matrix, blacklist filtering, de-duplication) unverified (P1, confidence 100)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new behavior (UI action + dialog in `BookingListItem.tsx`, new `AddGuestsDialog`, new `viewer.bookings.addGuests` mutation + handler with permission/blacklist/dedup logic, and new email templates + `sendAddGuestsEmails`) but the PR diff shows no corresponding test additions for this new logic/surface area. While we can’t prove no tests exist elsewhere in the repo, it’s a concrete, diff-grounded review gap that the new authorization/filtering behavior isn’t covered by tests in this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hideCalendarNotes is missing from the constructed CalendarEvent evt, unlike the scheduled-booking flow, causing private descriptions to leak in guest-add ICS attachments for event types configured to hide calendar notes (ADVISORY, P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the constructed `evt: CalendarEvent` includes `description: booking.description || ""` but does not include any `hideCalendarNotes`/equivalent flag (it’s not set anywhere in the new flow). The new add-guests email templates generate ICS via `generateIcsString({ event: this.calEvent, ... })`, so if ICS generation relies on a `hideCalendarNotes` field to suppress private notes (as the finding claims exists in the scheduled-booking flow), this add-guests path would leak the full `booking.description` into ICS attachments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Handler ignores seat capacity and never creates bookingSeat records for seated event types, allowing guests to be added and emailed while overfilling the slot and desynchronizing seat counts (ADVISORY, P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the new `addGuestsHandler` unconditionally appends new `attendees` via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` and then sends calendar/email updates. There is no logic in the diff to check `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or any capacity constraint) before adding guests, even though `evt.seatsPerTimeSlot` is populated later. The finding’s specific claim about not creating `bookingSeat` records cannot be verified from the diff (no such model/usage shown), but the broader issue—no seat/capacity handling for seated event types when adding attendees—is directly supported by the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failure is swallowed with console.log and the mutation still returns success, so the organizer sees a success toast when no emails or ICS updates were sent, with no partial-success signal (ADVISORY, P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending failures are caught and only `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` is executed, after which the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` and the client `onSuccess` toast (`showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`) will fire. This creates an unreported partial-success scenario for email delivery. However, the finding’s claim that “no ... ICS updates were sent” isn’t supported: `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is awaited *before* the try/catch and would throw (failing the mutation) if the calendar update/ICS handling failed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update runs with the calling user's credentials instead of the organizer's: when an attendee adds guests, updateCalendarAttendees executes with the attendee's calendar credentials against a calendar event they don't own, failing or being skipped while the DB write already committed (ADVISORY, P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation explicitly allows an attendee to call it (`const isAttendee = ...` and the permission check permits `isAttendee`). However the calendar sync is performed using the authenticated caller’s credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller), not the booking organizer. The calendar event being updated is for `booking.userId`/`organizer` (see `evt.organizer` built from organizer data). This mismatch means an attendee-triggered add could commit the DB attendee creation, then attempt `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` with the attendee’s credentials, which may not have access to update the organizer’s calendar event (leading to failure/skip while DB is already updated).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team-permission check uses && instead of ||: `isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId) && isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId)`; since a Membership has a single role, no user can be both ADMIN and OWNER, so team admins always get FORBIDDEN and the isTeamAdmin call is dead code (addGuests.handler.ts:42-44)

adjudication.rationale:
In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`:
```ts
const isTeamAdminOrOwner =
  (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) &&
  (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));
```
Given the later gate:
```ts
if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;
```
a user who is an admin (but not an owner), or an owner (but not an admin), will be denied unless they are also the organizer/attendee. This contradicts the variable name and likely intended “admin OR owner” permission check, causing incorrect FORBIDDEN responses for team admins/owners.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Handler grants mutation to any booking attendee and constructs EventManager with the caller's (ctx.user) credentials instead of the booking owner's, so an attendee can add guests and calendar updates run under the wrong account's credentials against the organizer's calendar reference (addGuests.handler.ts:46-51, 148-153)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization explicitly allows any attendee to perform the mutation (`const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the subsequent `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw ...`). The handler then builds the calendar update client using the *caller’s* credentials (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] }); await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`). If an attendee invokes this mutation, calendar updates will run under the attendee’s account rather than the booking owner/organizer, which is inconsistent with updating the organizer’s booking/destination calendar references included on `booking`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Booking query filters only on id with no status check, and ICS status is hardcoded to CONFIRMED in both email classes, allowing guests to be added to cancelled/rejected bookings and sending ICS REQUESTs that resurrect cancelled events in calendars (addGuests.handler.ts:26-50, organizer-add-guests-email.ts:19-20, attendee-add-guests-email.ts:12-16)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the booking is fetched purely by `id` (no additional constraint/guard in the diff) and the flow proceeds to update attendees and send calendar updates/emails. Separately, both new email templates hardcode an ICS `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"` (packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts and organizer-add-guests-email.ts), so if this mutation is invoked for a non-active booking (e.g., cancelled/rejected), the generated ICS would incorrectly re-confirm the event in recipients’ calendars. The hardcoded ICS status/method is directly verifiable in the diff; the lack of a booking-status gate is also directly shown, though the existence of a status field isn’t visible here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client and server schemas have drifted: the dialog's zod schema has a uniqueness .refine but ZAddGuestsInputSchema does not, and the handler only dedupes against existing attendees, never within the guests array, and compares case-sensitively while the blacklist lowercases; duplicate or case-variant emails insert duplicate Attendee rows causing duplicate ICS/email sends (addGuests.schema.ts:4-6, AddGuestsDialog.tsx:29-33, addGuests.handler.ts:59-66)
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the handler only filters against existing attendees/blacklist and does not deduplicate within the submitted guests array, allowing repeated (or case-variant) emails to create duplicate Attendee rows via createMany—same core issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklisted emails are silently filtered out while the handler still returns success and the dialog toasts guests_added, so the operator has no way to know some emails were dropped (addGuests.handler.ts:55-66)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` are filtered out when building `uniqueGuests` (guests are excluded if `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), but the mutation still succeeds as long as at least one guest remains (`if (uniqueGuests.length === 0) throw ...`). The UI (`AddGuestsDialog` onSuccess) always toasts `t("guests_added")` and closes, with no indication that some submitted emails were dropped. This is a verifiable partial-success/misleading-success behavior introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: For event types with seatsPerTimeSlot, createMany on attendees bypasses seat logic entirely, so seat caps are not enforced and recipients get AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the seat-booking email flow (addGuests.handler.ts:83-92)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the new `addGuests` mutation appends attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` without any check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` / seat availability, so it can add guests beyond any seat cap purely based on the DB write shown in the diff. Also, `sendAddGuestsEmails` explicitly sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to `newGuests` (`if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) ... AttendeeScheduledEmail`), with no branching for any seat-specific email flow in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The guests array is unbounded (z.array(z.string().email()) with no .max), allowing a single mutation to enqueue thousands of emails and createMany rows (addGuests.schema.ts:5)

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts). The handler then uses the provided array to `createMany` attendees (addGuests.handler.ts) and calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which can enqueue one or more emails per attendee (email-manager.ts). This allows a single request to create an unbounded number of DB rows and outbound emails, enabling DoS/spam behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dialog initializes multiEmailValue to [""] and 'Add another' appends "", which fails z.string().email() validation, so one leftover empty row blocks submission of otherwise-valid input with a misleading uniqueness error (AddGuestsDialog.tsx:38-47, MultiEmail.tsx:78-92)
matched_golden_ids: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that initializing/adding empty-string entries (e.g., [""] and appending "") causes validation problems in the multi-email flow, and imply the fix is to avoid starting with an empty string (use an empty array / handle empty state separately).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email-send error handler swallows the error object entirely (`catch { console.log(...) }` with no error argument), making email-delivery outages undebuggable (addGuests.handler.ts:168-172)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which catches exceptions and logs only a generic message without including `err`/stack/context. This reduces debuggability/observability for email delivery failures, but does not directly break booking/guest addition behavior (the handler continues and returns success regardless).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:33-35 - Team-permission check ANDs isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&, making the admin-or-owner gate unreachable for team ADMINs, causing them to receive FORBIDDEN when editing team bookings; should use || or a single role check

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&` between `isTeamAdmin(...)` and `isTeamOwner(...)`. That requires the user to be both an admin and an owner, so a team ADMIN (but not OWNER) will not satisfy this check and can hit the `FORBIDDEN` branch even though the variable name and finding describe an intended "admin OR owner" permission gate. Using `||` or a single role check would align with the expected access control.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:60-84 - Guest dedupe compares raw input case-sensitively with no canonical form and no unique DB constraint on (bookingId, email), allowing format drift duplicates (e.g. Guest@X.com vs guest@x.com) that create duplicate attendee rows, ics REQUESTs, and emails

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, deduping uses strict string equality against existing attendee emails (`guest === attendee.email`) and blacklist checks `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where the blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not. No canonicalization (e.g., `toLowerCase().trim()`) is applied to input or stored emails in this diff, so case-variant inputs like `Guest@X.com` can bypass both the existing-attendee check and the blacklist check, leading to duplicate attendee rows and downstream duplicate calendar/email effects. The claim about a missing DB unique constraint isn’t verifiable from this diff, but the case-sensitive dedupe issue itself is directly shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:60-84 - Check-then-insert dedupe has TOCTOU race: two concurrent addGuests calls can both observe the attendee absent and both insert duplicate attendee rows

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, deduping is done by reading `booking.attendees` (from an earlier `findFirst`) and filtering `guests` against that snapshot, then inserting via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails }}}})` without `skipDuplicates`, a transaction, or any locking. Two concurrent `addGuests` calls can both observe the same attendee email as absent and both attempt to insert it, leading to duplicate attendee rows (or an insert error if a unique DB constraint exists, which is not shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:66-84 + addGuests.schema.ts:4 - Guests array has no .max() cap, allowing an unbounded guest list that materializes 10k+ attendee rows, emails, and calendar payload in a single user-triggered request

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new authed mutation `addGuests` whose input schema (`ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in addGuests.schema.ts) allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler uses this array to (1) `createMany` attendee rows for all filtered emails and (2) build `attendeesList` and a `CalendarEvent` containing all attendees, then (3) calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which iterates over `calendarEvent.attendees` to send emails. With no `.max()` cap, a single request can materialize an arbitrarily large number of DB rows and outbound side effects (calendar updates + many emails), creating a resource-exhaustion/abuse vector grounded directly in the added code paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:16-24 - Booking fetch has no status guard and templates hardcode CONFIRMED/REQUEST, so guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, sending ics REQUEST emails that re-accept cancelled events on attendees' calendars

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the booking is fetched only by `id` (no constraint/guard on booking state), so the mutation can run for any booking record it can access. The newly added email templates (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts`, `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`) unconditionally generate an ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"`. If the underlying booking is cancelled/rejected/otherwise not confirmed, this can send calendar REQUEST updates that misrepresent the event state to attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:150-155 - Calendar update uses the requesting user's credentials, so when an attendee (permitted via isAttendee branch) calls the mutation, updateCalendarAttendees runs with empty credentials and the organizer's calendar event attendee list never updates, diverging from the DB

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the calendar sync is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, i.e., using the *requesting* user’s credentials rather than the booking organizer’s (`booking.user` is included with `credentials` but never used). Since the mutation explicitly allows an attendee to call it (`const isAttendee = ...`), an attendee-triggered call can run `updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` without organizer credentials, meaning external calendar updates for the organizer (and possibly the event itself) may not occur even though the DB attendees were updated via `prisma.booking.update(...)`, causing inconsistency.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:15-18 - Dialog re-declares an inline zod schema instead of importing the shared ZAddGuestsInputSchema, and the copies already disagree on uniqueness semantics, risking client/server drift

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the client defines an inline `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` as `z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` enforcing uniqueness, while the server router imports `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` from `addGuests.schema.ts` which is `z.object({ bookingId: z.number(), guests: z.array(z.string().email()) })` with no uniqueness constraint. This is a real, diff-grounded inconsistency (and the client isn’t even reusing the shared schema), creating client/server validation drift even if it may not immediately break the UI path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:33-35 - Permission check performs two sequential DB round-trips (isTeamAdmin then isTeamOwner) hitting the same membership row; a single membership fetch resolving the role once would remove a query and prevent role-combination mistakes

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the permission flag is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which both (a) performs two separate async checks and (b) contradicts the variable name `isTeamAdminOrOwner` by requiring the user to be *both* admin and owner. This can incorrectly deny access to legitimate team admins/owners and is grounded directly in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Permission gate in addGuests.handler.ts allows any logged-in attendee of a booking to mutate it, not just the organizer or team admins, expanding the trust model without accepted intent (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization explicitly permits any authenticated attendee to add guests: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and the guard only rejects when `!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee` (so `isAttendee` passes). This means a non-organizer attendee can mutate the booking’s attendee list via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, which is a concrete privilege expansion/security issue visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update in addGuests.handler.ts runs with the caller's credentials via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user), so when an attendee triggers the mutation, updateCalendarAttendees is invoked with the attendee's calendar credentials against the organizer's event, and the organizer's calendar never gets the new attendees (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed using an `EventManager` instantiated from `ctx.user` (the mutation caller) and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (`const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] }); await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`). Since the mutation explicitly allows non-organizers (`isAttendee`) to call it, this design means the calendar update will run under attendee credentials when an attendee adds guests. The diff does not show what `EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` actually does (e.g., whether it also updates organizer calendars via booking/user data), so the claim that the organizer calendar "never" gets updated is not strictly verifiable from the diff alone, but the review concern about credential/actor mismatch is diff-grounded and potentially impactful.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, requiring a user to be both admin and owner, effectively rejecting non-owner team admins while accepting any attendee; the permission hierarchy is inverted relative to the intended admin-or-owner pattern (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both an admin and an owner. Given the variable name and typical permission intent (“admin OR owner”), this will incorrectly deny non-owner team admins. This directly affects the authorization gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)`, making the check stricter than intended for team admins.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Handler never checks booking.status, so guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, or pending bookings and receive hard-CONFIRMED REQUEST ics invites that re-confirm a cancelled meeting (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `addGuestsHandler` (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`), the booking is fetched and updated without any check of `booking.status` (it isn’t even selected/used). The handler will proceed to `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and then send emails. The new email templates (`packages/emails/templates/*add-guests-email.ts`) generate ICS payloads with `status: "CONFIRMED"` and `method: "REQUEST"`, meaning this endpoint can send confirmation-style invites even for cancelled/rejected/pending bookings. This is a correctness bug enabled by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Silent contract drift between client and server: server silently filters duplicate and blacklisted emails from guests and returns success, while the client enforces uniqueness and shows a success toast, so users are told guests were added when they were silently dropped (P2)

adjudication.rationale: Server-side `addGuestsHandler` filters out guests that are already attendees and those in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` via `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)` and proceeds to return success as long as `uniqueGuests.length > 0`, without reporting any dropped emails. Client `AddGuestsDialog` always shows a generic success toast (`t("guests_added")`) on mutation success and does not account for blacklist/existing-attendee drops, so users can be told "Guests added" even if some provided emails were ignored. However, the finding’s mention of server filtering *duplicate inputs* isn’t supported by the diff (server doesn’t dedupe within `guests`; client enforces uniqueness).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email delivery failure in addGuests.handler.ts is swallowed with only a console.log after the DB write, so callers are told guests were added and the cache is invalidated even when guests receive no email or ics invite (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch { console.log(...) }` and the handler still returns success (`return { message: "Guests added" };`) after the DB update and calendar update. This means callers/UI will treat the operation as successful (and the web UI invalidates bookings cache on success) even if notification/ICS delivery fails, with the failure effectively swallowed (only a `console.log`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx and addGuests.schema.ts maintain two independently hand-maintained Zod schemas for the same input that have already diverged (client has uniqueness refine, server doesn't), requiring future validation changes to be made twice (P3)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two separate Zod validations for the same “add guests” input: `apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx` defines a local `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (an array of emails with a uniqueness `.refine`), while the server defines `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` as `{ bookingId: number; guests: email[] }` without the uniqueness constraint. This is duplicated, independently maintained validation that has already diverged (client stricter than server), creating an ongoing maintenance/inconsistency risk when rules change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New guests are assigned timeZone and locale from the organizer rather than guest-derived values, so persisted attendee records carry misleading timezone data that future features trusting attendee.timeZone will inherit (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, newly created attendee records are populated with `timeZone: organizer.timeZone` and `locale: organizer.locale` for each added guest (`guestsFullDetails` mapping). Since the UI only collects email addresses, there is no guest-derived timezone/locale available, so this isn’t a verifiable functional defect from the diff alone. However, it does concretely introduce potentially misleading persisted data (attendee timezone/locale reflecting organizer rather than the guest), which could affect future features that rely on `attendee.timeZone`/`attendee.locale` being the attendee’s actual values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email blacklist normalization mismatch in addGuests.handler.ts: blacklist entries are lowercased but incoming guest email is compared un-normalized, allowing bypass via case variation

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS are normalized via `.toLowerCase()`, but the incoming `guest` value is compared as-is: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Because `guest` is not lowercased/trimmed before comparison, a blacklisted email can bypass the filter by varying letter case (e.g., `Bad@Example.com`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic error in addGuests.handler.ts: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && instead of ||, requiring callers to be both team admin AND team owner, blocking non-owner admins

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the caller to be both a team admin and a team owner. Given the variable name and typical permission models, this likely should be `||` so that either admins or owners can add guests. As written, non-owner admins will be incorrectly denied (`FORBIDDEN`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Trust-the-client authz in addGuests.handler.ts: any attendee of any booking permanently retains add-guests rights with no booking.status check or cap, enabling emails with organizer identity and video-call URL to arbitrary addresses

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuests` mutation allows any authenticated user who is an existing attendee (`isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((a) => a.email === user.email)`) to add arbitrary guest emails to that booking, with no check on booking state (no `booking.status`/cancellation/ended check) and no cap/rate limit in the handler. The handler builds a `CalendarEvent` including `videoCallData` from `booking.references` and then calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, which can propagate organizer/event details (potentially including video call URL) to the newly provided addresses. This is a real authz/security issue exposed by the diff (even though “trust-the-client” is imprecise wording, the over-broad attendee permission is in the server code).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Guests array is unbounded (z.array without max) and endpoint has no rate limit, creating an email-bombing vector against arbitrary third-party addresses

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC mutation `addGuests` accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound (`addGuests.schema.ts`) and the handler will send emails after updating attendees (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` in `addGuests.handler.ts`). The UI (`MultiEmail`) allows adding an arbitrary number of email fields. There is no per-request cap or throttling logic in the router/handler shown, and any organizer/attendee/team admin/owner can invoke it, enabling a large guest list (or repeated calls) to trigger mass outbound email to arbitrary addresses.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side dedup of guests against existing attendees is case-sensitive and doesn't dedup within input, causing duplicate attendee rows and duplicate email sends

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server filters `uniqueGuests` only by exact string match against existing attendees (`guest === attendee.email`) and does not normalize case, so `Test@x.com` vs `test@x.com` will be treated as different. It also does not deduplicate within the `guests` input array at all (server schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` allows duplicates; only the client dialog has a local uniqueness refine), so repeated emails in `guests` can reach `createMany`. That can lead to duplicate attendee records (if the DB allows it) or a constraint error, and in either case the subsequent email logic can produce duplicate notifications if duplicate attendees are created.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking.status check before mutating: guests can be added to cancelled or rejected bookings, sending REQUEST/CONFIRMED ics invites that silently resuscitate cancelled meetings

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the booking is fetched and then always updated (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`) and calendar/email side effects are triggered (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails`). There is no check of any `booking.status`/cancellation state before mutating or before generating ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` / `method: "REQUEST"` (see `attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`). The UI also adds an "additional_guests" action unconditionally in `BookingListItem.tsx`. So, based on the diff, cancelled/rejected bookings could still be modified and trigger CONFIRMED/REQUEST invites.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side email validation schema in AddGuestsDialog.tsx is a duplicated copy of ZAddGuestsInputSchema, causing client/server drift risk and misleading BAD_REQUEST errors when they diverge; should import the shared schema instead

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the client defines its own `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (`z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)`) instead of using the server’s `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` in `addGuests.schema.ts` (an object `{ bookingId, guests }` with no uniqueness refinement). This is diff-verifiable duplication/mismatch that can drift over time and leads to inconsistent validation rules between client and server (e.g., uniqueness is enforced client-side but not in the shared server schema).

adjudication_records.issue_text: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx onError, the fallback `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` is dead code because the template string message is always non-empty, making the fallback toast unreachable; the condition should be restructured so the fallback is reachable

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `onError` builds `message` with a template literal: ``const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;``. Template literals always return a string; even when values are `undefined`/empty, the result will be non-empty (e.g., `"undefined: "`). Therefore `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` will never hit the fallback, making it unreachable and preventing the intended generic error toast from ever being shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts swallows all email send failures with a non-error console.log and still returns success, decoupling the success response from the email side effect; the catch should log the actual error and surface failure in the response

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation wraps `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` in a `try/catch` that only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` and then still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This is verifiably true from the diff and is a concrete observability/architecture concern (email side-effect failures are silently ignored and the actual error isn’t logged), but the diff does not prove that the API must fail when emails fail, so it’s not a definite correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dual-write gap: attendees are committed to the DB before the calendar update in addGuests.handler.ts:95-105, and a calendar failure leaves persisted state inconsistent with no rollback or compensation

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code persists new attendees to the DB via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` before calling `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. There is no surrounding transaction or compensating delete if the calendar update throws. Since `createMany` commits immediately, a calendar failure would return an error while leaving the DB updated (and calendars not), creating an inconsistent state as described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Retry after a partial calendar failure is blocked: the dedupe filter (uniqueGuests) excludes emails already in booking.attendees, causing emails_must_be_unique_valid errors and wedging the feature for those guests (never added to calendar, never invited)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the DB is updated first via prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...). Only after that does it call await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking). If updateCalendarAttendees throws (e.g., calendar sync failure), the mutation aborts after having persisted the new attendees. A subsequent retry with the same guest emails will be filtered out by uniqueGuests (it excludes emails already present in booking.attendees), leading to uniqueGuests.length === 0 and a BAD_REQUEST ("emails_must_be_unique_valid"). This makes it impossible to retry calendar/invite updates for those already-persisted guests, matching the reported wedged behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email send failure is silently swallowed by catch with console.log, so guests can be persisted with no invite ever sent while the user is told 'Guests added'

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, guests are persisted via `prisma.booking.update(... createMany ...)` and the handler returns success regardless of email outcome. The email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch { console.log(...) }`, which swallows failures and does not throw, so the TRPC mutation still succeeds and the UI `onSuccess` shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")`. This can lead to guests being added while no notification/invite email is sent, yet the user is told it succeeded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive dedupe in addGuests.handler.ts:78-85 allows duplicate attendee rows for the same person; no unique constraint on (bookingId, email) in the base schema

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `uniqueGuests` filters with strict equality (`guest === attendee.email`) and only lowercases the blacklist list, not the incoming `guests` or existing attendee emails. This makes dedupe effectively case-sensitive, so inputs like `Alice@X.com` vs `alice@x.com` can bypass the filter and be inserted via `attendees.createMany`, creating duplicate attendee rows (or causing a DB error if a unique constraint exists, which is not shown in this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side Set check in AddGuestsDialog.tsx only dedupes within one dialog session, not against persisted attendees across sessions or case variants, so it doesn't mitigate the duplicate-attendee issue

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, the local `ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(z.string().email()).refine(...)` only checks uniqueness within the currently entered `multiEmailValue` (one dialog interaction) and does not compare against existing/persisted attendees. The server handler does attempt to filter existing attendees (`!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`), so the client-side Set check is not the primary protection and indeed doesn’t address cross-session/persisted duplicates (or case-variant duplicates). This is a real, diff-grounded validation/UX gap, but not a clearly broken behavior by itself because the server is responsible for enforcing constraints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklisted/duplicate guests are silently dropped in addGuests.handler.ts:72-85 while the caller is told 'Guests added', a false organizer-facing success report (silent mismatch between reported and actual data)

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler filters the requested `guests` into `uniqueGuests` by removing emails that are already attendees and any in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` (uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)). If `uniqueGuests` is non-empty, it proceeds to add only those via `createMany`, but still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` and the UI shows `t("guests_added")` without indicating partial failure. So some requested emails can be ignored while the caller receives an unqualified success, which is a real diff-grounded UX/behavior concern (though not necessarily a hard functional defect if partial-success is intended).

adjudication_records.issue_text: New guests are written with name: "" and the organizer's timeZone/locale in addGuests.handler.ts:106-120, persisting incorrect data (wrong timezone) for the guest with no way to correct it, misclassifying the row from creation

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new attendees are persisted with `name: ""` and `timeZone`/`locale` copied from the organizer (lines creating `guestsFullDetails`). Those stored fields are then used when building `attendeesList` for emails (`timeZone: attendee.timeZone`, translation via `attendee.locale`). Since the UI only collects guest emails (no timezone/locale), this diff causes added guests to receive persisted timezone/locale that likely does not match the guest, with no correction path shown in the diff—impacting correctness of attendee data and potentially email date/locale formatting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:81-83 uses && instead of || for team admin/owner permission check, wrongly rejecting team admins who are not owners (and vice versa) with FORBIDDEN

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. Given the variable name and its use in the permission gate (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN;`), this will incorrectly forbid legitimate team admins who are not owners (and owners who are not admins) from adding guests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:118-127 commits DB attendee write before calendar update with no rollback or error handling, leaving partial state on calendar failure

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the DB is updated first via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` (around the reported lines), and only afterwards `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` is called with no surrounding transaction/rollback. If the calendar update throws, the mutation will fail but the attendee rows have already been persisted, leaving the system in a partial/inconsistent state (DB shows new guests, external calendar/invites may not).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:88 dedup filter makes retries of failed calendar sync impossible — persisted guests are excluded so retry throws 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' BAD_REQUEST

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the DB is updated first (prisma.booking.update with attendees.createMany) and only afterwards it calls eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking) without a try/catch or transaction. If calendar sync throws, the mutation fails but guests have already been persisted; a retry with the same emails will be filtered out by uniqueGuests (excluded if already in booking.attendees) and then throws BAD_REQUEST when uniqueGuests.length === 0. This matches the finding and is directly implied by the diff’s ordering.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:151-154 email failure silently swallowed with bare console.log (no error object, bookingId, or stack), user sees 'Guests added' success toast while no notifications or ICS updates were sent

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which swallows the error and logs no `err`, `bookingId`, or stack, while still returning `{ message: "Guests added" }` (and the UI toasts success on mutation success). However, the finding’s claim that “no … ICS updates were sent” isn’t supported because `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs *before* the try/catch and would still execute (or throw) independently of email sending.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:41-44 error message template literal is always truthy, making the t('unable_to_add_guests') fallback dead code and showing 'undefined:' prefix toast on errors without data.code

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal is always a truthy string, so the fallback `t("unable_to_add_guests")` is unreachable. If `err.data?.code` is missing, the toast will show an `undefined:` prefix (e.g. `"undefined: <translated message>"`), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:71-73 findFirstOrThrow on nullable booking.userId surfaces an unhandled Prisma P2025 500 error instead of the promised NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN/BAD_REQUEST TRPCError shapes

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. Since `booking.userId` is treated as nullable/optional (explicit `|| 0`), a booking with `userId = null` will query `id=0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (Prisma “record not found”, e.g. P2025). This exception is not converted into the handler’s intended `TRPCError` shapes (`NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`/`BAD_REQUEST`), so it will surface as an unhandled 500.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:158-163 EventManager built from acting user's credentials instead of the organizer's, so calendar update silently no-ops when a non-organizer adds guests while reporting success

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, the handler permits non-organizers (team admin/owner or an existing attendee) to add guests, but it builds the EventManager using the acting user (`...user`) and credentials fetched from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` rather than the booking organizer (`booking.user`/`organizer`). Since the calendar update call `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` is unconditional, this can result in updating the wrong calendar account or doing nothing when the actor has no calendar credentials, while still returning success. The diff even fetches `booking.user.credentials` but never uses them, supporting that organizer credentials were likely intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.schema.ts:5 guests array has no .max() cap, allowing unbounded payload to amplify into N attendee rows, N emails, and per-attendee calendar writes

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`, `guests` is `z.array(z.string().email())` with no upper bound. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, each entry can translate into a DB row via `attendees.createMany` and then triggers fan-out work: `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` (with `evt.attendees` including all attendees) and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which sends emails over `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)`. Without a `.max()` cap, an attacker with access to this mutation could submit a very large array to amplify into many attendee rows/emails/calendar updates (resource exhaustion).

adjudication_records.issue_text: addGuests.handler.ts:86-94 dedup/blacklist email comparisons are case-sensitive while blacklist is lowercased, allowing duplicate attendees and blacklist bypass by changing case

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the blacklist array is normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS...map(...toLowerCase())`), but the comparisons use the raw `guest` string without normalization: duplicates are checked via `guest === attendee.email` and blacklist via `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Because both are case-sensitive, a user can bypass the blacklist or add a duplicate attendee by changing email casing (e.g., `Test@x.com` vs `test@x.com`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema does not enforce uniqueness within the guests input array, so direct API calls with duplicate strings insert duplicate rows via createMany

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness. In `addGuestsHandler`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not dedupe within the provided `guests` array itself, so a direct API call like `["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` will pass validation and be sent to `attendees.createMany({ data: guestsFullDetails })`, potentially inserting duplicate attendee rows (or causing a DB error depending on constraints not shown in the diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog.tsx:30-36 isInvalidEmail is never reset on success or dialog re-open, showing stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' warning over untouched input

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed validation in `handleAdd`, but it is not reset in the success path of `addGuestsMutation.onSuccess` (which only closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`). Since the dialog component stays mounted (it’s always rendered in `BookingListItem` and only toggled via `open`), reopening after a previous validation failure can show the stale `emails_must_be_unique_valid` warning over a fresh/untouched input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: organizer-add-guests-email.ts:30 replyTo header grows unboundedly with attendee count across repeated add-guests calls, eventually causing MTAs to reject or clip the message

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the organizer email sets `replyTo` to an array containing the organizer plus **all** attendee emails: `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`. Since `addGuests.handler.ts` rebuilds `evt.attendees` from the persisted booking attendees after each add, the attendee list (and thus `replyTo`) can grow with each subsequent add-guests call. The diff does not prove MTAs will reject/clip, but it does introduce an unbounded header-growth/deliverability risk tied directly to attendee count.
